title: WordScript Regression Transcript Corpus
description: Schema for fixture entries that drive transcription-bias and correction-guardrail regression tests. Each entry is a reproducer for one observed failure mode, used by corpus-driven unit tests.

version.description: Corpus schema version. Bump on incompatible changes.

id.description: snake_case identifier unique within the corpus

vocabulary.description: Individual terms. Granular profile context for every LLM stage, and the input to deterministic repair. No spoken form -- a term has no reliable left-hand side (ADR 0033).

raw_transcript.description: What STT (or simulated STT) actually delivered before AI cleanup

biased_correction.description: The reply the correction model returned. Present only where a guardrail is under test: corpus_drives_correction_guardrail_assertions runs it through normalize_correction and asserts expected_post_correction. With expected_guardrail null the reply must survive byte-identical, which is how a guardrail is kept from growing teeth it was never meant to have.

expected_transcription_bias.description: Expected outcome of the bias analysis path before correction. The profile context field is not part of it: it holds topics and never reaches the recognizer (ADR 0032).

language.description: Profile language the detection stage compares against. Absent means auto-detect, which never permits a language-based strip.

language_locked.description: Whether the language is pinned. It only lowers the corroboration the drift check needs from two independent signals to one, never to zero.

low_confidence_segments.description: Whether the confidence gate upstream rejected a segment. One of the signals that can corroborate a language mismatch.

expected_detection.description: Expected outcome of the post-STT detection stage, which runs on the raw transcript before any AI cleanup.

unchanged.description: Assert the transcript comes back byte-identical and no rule altered it. This is how the legitimate-multilingual-dictation guarantee is pinned.

expected_vocabulary_repair.description: What deterministic repair must do to raw_transcript. Negative cases carry the same shape with text equal to the input, and they are the ones that matter: a missed repair is readable text, a wrong one is a word the user never said (ADR 0033).

applied.description: Terms whose repair must be reported. Empty asserts nothing was applied.

expected_vocabulary_candidates.description: Terms vocabulary_learning must read out of the raw_transcript / expected_post_correction pair, in order. An empty array is an assertion, not an omission: rewording, filler removal, sentence restructuring and capitalization must all yield nothing, and a term the profile already carries is a hit rather than a find (ADR 0035).

expected_post_correction.description: What the user should see after Transform runs. Usually the raw transcript when a guardrail fires.

expected_guardrail.description: Name of the applied_rules entry expected from normalize_correction. Null when no guardrail fires.

notes.description: Free-form explanation of the failure mode for the next reader. Anonymize any real customer data.
